title: Over-Tightening Threaded Plastic Fittings
description: Educational breakdown showing how excessive PTFE tape and wrench force split tapered plastic pipe fittings due to internal hoop stress.
image_prompt: A detailed, crisp professional close-up visual of a white schedule 40 PVC female threaded adapter connected to a male threaded fitting. A visible longitudinal hairline crack runs down the collar of the female fitting caused by stress expansion. Flakes of white PTFE tape are neatly visible around the exposed threads. The background is an authentic clean residential plumbing workspace under a sink with realistic lighting, soft depth of field, focused sharply on the threaded fitting assembly. Vertical 9:16 aspect ratio composition, photorealistic texture of plastic, realistic pipe geometry, clear educational detail. No text, no labels, no logos, no watermarks, no brand names, no fake badges.
visual_story: The visual focuses directly on the point of failure: a cracked female plastic adapter socket. Viewers can see how excess thread sealant tape built up inside the tapered NPT joint, acting as a wedge. As the fitting was turned deeper, outward expansion pressure split the plastic collar along its stress axis.

on_image_text.hook: Over-Tightening Plastic Threads Causes Hidden Cracks
on_image_text.explanation: Tapered threads wedge outward; excessive tape and leverage create hoop stress that splits female plastic fittings.
on_image_text.callout: Socket Split From Outward Radial Pressure
on_image_text.takeaway: Hand-tighten plastic NPT joints, then turn 1 to 2 full turns with a wrench using plastic-safe thread sealant.
